findings.title: Pin and verify the downloaded installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: This follows redirects and pipes arbitrary network content directly into sh. A compromised origin, DNS/redirect path, or altered installer can execute arbitrary commands during every image build and embed a compromised artifact in the image.

findings.title: Keep Run synchronous or wait for spawned sends
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, Run returned only after every result was sent. It now returns immediately after starting goroutines. A caller that safely closes results after Run returns can now race with these sends and panic with "send on closed channel"; receivers can also observe Run completion before any result is available.

findings.title: Require both admin status and tenant match for deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: The new OR condition returns true for a non-admin whose tenant matches the record, and for an admin targeting a record in another tenant. Either case bypasses the previous cross-tenant/admin authorization boundary and permits unauthorized deletion.

findings.title: Implement the clamping promised by clampPercent
findings.whyItBreaks: `clampPercent(101, 100)` returns 101, despite the exported name promising a bounded percentage. Consumers may rely on that contract for safe progress-bar sizing; the adjacent `progressBar` then computes a negative repeat count and throws.

findings.title: Propagate invalid-settings errors instead of returning defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: This exported parser previously signaled malformed JSON and invalid field types by throwing. It now returns a valid-looking default Settings value for every failure, so callers cannot distinguish a parse failure from a user who actually chose the default settings. In particular, updateFontSize will save a new default-theme document after an invalid input rather than aborting, overwriting the original persisted value.

findings.title: Count the final partial page
findings.whyItBreaks: For totals not evenly divisible by pageSize, Math.floor drops the page containing remaining items. For example, 11 items at a size of 10 returns 1 instead of 2, so pagination consumers cannot navigate to the final item.

facts.meaning: The page count rounds down instead of up.
A remainder/partial final page is omitted or a small result becomes zero pages.

findings.title: Use the requested branch’s commit for artifacts
findings.whyItBreaks: `builtFrom` remains the commit resolved from `branch`, but `artifacts` now come from the separate `verified` ref. A caller requesting a report for one branch can receive artifacts from a different commit, producing an internally inconsistent report.

findings.title: Restore the requested limit
findings.whyItBreaks: For every positive limit, this returns every reversed entry rather than at most limit entries. renderFeed passes 20, then writes each returned entry into its output array, so feeds with more than 20 entries exceed the intended page size.

findings.title: Restore the exclusive first-day-of-next-month boundary
findings.whyItBreaks: `Date.UTC(year, month, 0)` resolves to midnight UTC at the start of the month's final day, while `contains` uses an exclusive end (`t < range.end.getTime()`) at src/lib/date-range.ts:32. Consequently, monthlyRevenue's inclusion predicate at src/reports/monthly.ts:17 rejects every non-void invoice issued on that final day, and exported CSV totals inherit the undercount.

facts.meaning: monthRange's end is now day 0 of the following month (the requested month's last day at midnight) instead of the first day of the next month.
Records on the last day of a month fall outside the half-open range and are omitted from monthly totals.

findings.title: Count only emitted manifest rows
findings.whyItBreaks: Stale entries are removed from rows, but `# entry-count` still uses `entries.length`. A manifest with one live and one stale entry declares two entries while containing one data row, breaking consumers that use the header to validate or parse the manifest.

findings.title: Preserve FormatLegacyID for compatibility
findings.whyItBreaks: FormatLegacyID is exported, so removing it makes existing consumers that generate or parse LEG-prefixed IDs fail to compile on upgrade. There is no replacement or deprecation shim in this change.

findings.title: Preserve the shippingQuote export
findings.whyItBreaks: shippingQuote was an exported function in this module but is deleted rather than re-exported under its existing name. Any consumer importing shippingQuote from src/orders will fail to compile or load after upgrading.

findings.title: Restore execute's declared string result
findings.whyItBreaks: Every call to the public execute(input): string API now throws "always fails" and cannot return the transformed string promised by its signature.

findings.title: Preserve viewer read-only handling
findings.whyItBreaks: An active viewer with fewer than five attempts previously passed isEligible and handle returned "read-only" at line 25. The new role check rejects that same request at line 24, making the explicit read-only branch unreachable.

findings.title: Keep draft saves independent of payment
findings.whyItBreaks: For a draft with payment="missing", the new predicate evaluates false. saveDraft therefore returns "blocked", even though saving an unpaid draft must remain possible.

findings.title: Read snapshot files from the requested commit
findings.whyItBreaks: publishSnapshot records commit=repo.headCommit(channel) but obtains files from repo.headCommit("stable"). Publishing any channel whose head differs from stable produces a self-inconsistent Snapshot: its commit and files describe different revisions. It also introduces a failure for repositories without a stable ref.

findings.title: Honor the public limit parameter
findings.whyItBreaks: `build(prefix, limit=3)` still returns ten entries because the body hard-codes `max_count = 10`. The public parameter promises that callers can control the returned result count.

findings.title: Validate that parsed integers are positive
findings.whyItBreaks: `parse_positive_int("-1")` returns `-1` and `parse_positive_int("0")` returns `0`, contradicting its public name. The unchanged caller then turns a negative amount into negative cents (`charge("-1") == -100`) instead of rejecting invalid input.

findings.title: Keep the CI workflow under .github/workflows
findings.whyItBreaks: GitHub Actions discovers workflows only in .github/workflows. This rename leaves the head tree with no workflow files, so pushes and pull requests no longer run npm ci, lint, or tests despite README.md stating that CI runs on every push.

findings.title: Enforce positivity or restore the neutral parser name
findings.whyItBreaks: `parse_positive_int("-5")` returns `-5` and `parse_positive_int("0")` returns `0`, contradicting its public positive-integer contract. Its caller consequently permits `charge("-5")` to produce `-500`.

findings.title: Borrow items when logging it
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items);` evaluates and consumes the `Vec<String>`; the subsequent `items.len()` attempts to borrow a moved value, causing Rust error E0382 and preventing the crate from compiling.

findings.title: Compute changed paths from the advertised base revision
findings.whyItBreaks: `fromRevision` remains the revision resolved from `pinnedTag`, but `changedPaths` is computed from `latest`. When those tags differ, consumers replay a path set relative to `latest` onto `pinnedTag`, violating the exported Changeset contract and potentially omitting changes between the pinned revision and latest.

findings.title: Update queries to use the renamed column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration, `users.email` no longer exists, but `src/query.sql:1` still executes `SELECT email FROM users`. Any upgraded deployment running that query receives a missing-column SQL error.

findings.title: Preserve the missing billing-key failure signal
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the environment lookup and its error means an unset or incorrectly provisioned BILLING_API_KEY is no longer detectable: makeClient always returns a client using the committed credential. Callers and deployments can no longer distinguish valid secret provisioning from configuration failure.

findings.title: Require administrators before purging projects
findings.whyItBreaks: `user.isAdmin=true` now returns `forbidden`, while `user.isAdmin=false` with an archived project reaches `db.delete`. This reverses the prior authorization policy and grants non-admins destructive access to archived projects.

facts.meaning: The refactored guard incorrectly returns forbidden for administrators.
Non-administrators can reach the destructive project purge/delete path.

findings.title: Restore handling for a missing settings file
findings.whyItBreaks: `load_settings` returns `None` for a nonexistent path (app/config.py:6-7). The removed fallback previously replaced that value with default workers; now `settings["workers"]` raises `TypeError`, so startup fails instead of using its established defaults.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures
findings.whyItBreaks: When Gateway.Submit fails, Charge logs the error and returns nil at line 19. Callers therefore cannot distinguish a completed charge from a rejected or failed payment and may treat an unpaid order as paid.

findings.title: Restore tenant scoping to the settings cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: settingsFor still fetches values by tenantId, but its cache key now contains only name. After tenant A fetches a setting named X, tenant B requesting X receives tenant A’s cached value without calling store.fetch, causing cross-tenant configuration leakage and incorrect behavior.

findings.title: Preserve the exported invalidate call signature
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing JavaScript callers using invalidate(tenantId, name) now have their second argument ignored and delete settings:<tenantId> rather than the cached setting. TypeScript callers fail to compile. This leaves settings stale for existing consumers after upgrade.

findings.title: Preserve the existing synchronous Inventory API
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing consumers can no longer construct Inventory without a Store, and reserve now returns a Promise rather than the prior boolean. JavaScript callers using `if (inventory.reserve(sku))` will treat the Promise as truthy even when the eventual result is false; TypeScript callers fail to compile.

findings.title: Serialize reservations for the same SKU
findings.whyItBreaks: The await splits the availability check from the in-memory decrement. With stock 1, two concurrent calls both read 1, both save 0, and both return true, so two consumers reserve one unit while persisted and in-memory stock show 0.

findings.title: Remove the duplicated retry delay conversion
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff now returns milliseconds (1,000 on attempt 0), but retry still multiplies it by 1,000 before passing it to sleep. The first retry waits 1,000,000 ms (16m40s) instead of 1 second, and capped retries wait 30,000,000 ms instead of 30 seconds.

findings.title: Return the file-close error from Save
findings.whyItBreaks: The deferred f.Close() error is discarded. A successful w.Flush() now makes Save return nil even when closing the output file fails; the prior implementation returned that error. Callers therefore cannot distinguish a completed save from a close-time I/O failure.

findings.title: Include the final row in each page
findings.whyItBreaks: The half-open bounds helper returns end as the exclusive endpoint, but range(start, end - 1) excludes both end and the final valid index. Thus a one-row page is empty and each larger page loses its last row; render_page and summarize expose the incomplete results.

findings.title: Return entries while they are within the TTL
findings.whyItBreaks: Immediately after set(), elapsed time is below ttlMs, so the new `>` condition deletes the fresh entry and returns null. Once elapsed time exceeds ttlMs, it instead returns the expired value indefinitely.

findings.title: Do not splice while iterating forward through jobs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing a completed job shifts the next job into its index, but forEach advances to the following index. For `[doneA, doneB]`, doneA is removed at index 0 and doneB is skipped, so pruneDone returns a completed job.

findings.title: Preserve the empty-input average
findings.whyItBreaks: When rows is empty, total is 0 and rows.length is 0, so this returns NaN instead of the prior numeric result 0. Consumers cannot safely use the result in arithmetic, display, or serialization.

findings.title: Avoid mutating the caller's rows
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.prototype.sort mutates rows in place. The prior implementation sorted a copy, so callers that reuse rows now silently observe it reordered after calling busiest().

findings.title: Sort scores numerically before reversing
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.prototype.sort() compares scores as strings. With input [{name:'nine',score:9},{name:'hundred',score:100}] and n=1, rankScores returns [9,100], so cutoff is 9 and topPlayers returns the first input player (score 9) instead of score 100.

findings.title: Restore constant-time webhook signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: Plain string equality may exit on the first differing character, allowing an attacker who can repeatedly submit webhook requests and measure response timing to progressively guess a valid HMAC. The prior hmac.compare_digest call specifically prevents this signature-oracle behavior.

findings.title: Keep balance updates inside the transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction exits and commits the ledger insert at line 23 before `_apply_balances` runs. If either balance UPDATE fails, `transfer` raises after a durable ledger record exists but before one or both account balances are updated, producing an inconsistent transfer.

findings.title: Preserve UTC when deriving the billing day
findings.whyItBreaks: The prior public behavior derived the date with getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate. The new local-time getters return a different billing day for instants near midnight in any non-UTC host timezone; for example, 2026-10-15T20:00:00Z becomes 2026-10-16 in Asia/Taipei instead of 2026-10-15. This can split or merge billing records based on server deployment timezone.

findings.title: Keep tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After tenant A reads account X, a read for tenant B and account X finds the same `memo` entry and returns tenant A's Profile without calling `fetchProfile`. This leaks/corrupts tenant-scoped profile results.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors from load
findings.whyItBreaks: A missing Map entry previously threw `missing: <key>`, but now returns `""`, which is a valid stored value. `loadAll` consequently returns a seemingly successful array with missing entries silently substituted, so callers cannot distinguish absent data from intentionally empty data.

findings.title: Preserve compatibility for existing retry Config callers
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing callers passing the previously required `{ maxAttempts, timeoutMs }` no longer type-check because `retries` and `timeout` are required. JavaScript callers instead receive `config.timeout === undefined`; line 8 produces a NaN deadline, and the timeout guard never expires, so retries can run beyond their configured timeout.

findings.title: Make retryBackground actually run off the caller path
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported name promises background behavior, but the implementation synchronously loops and invokes `fn()` before returning. Consumers using it to keep a request or UI path non-blocking will instead block for every retry attempt.

findings.title: Report final retryBackground failure to callers
findings.whyItBreaks: After every attempt fails, the new exported function returns `void` exactly as it does on success. Callers cannot distinguish exhausted retries from a completed operation and may treat a failed background operation as successful.

findings.title: Support numeric Field values before accepting them
findings.whyItBreaks: FieldProps now accepts number, but value.length is invalid for number. TypeScript reports an error on this implementation; if emitted without type checking, <Field value={42} /> renders "len=undefined" instead of a valid label.

findings.title: Retain a buffer large enough for generated patches
findings.whyItBreaks: `git()` produces the full patch at line 140. Without `maxBuffer`, `spawnSync` uses Node's 1 MiB default; a PR whose diff exceeds that limit is terminated and `git()` throws, so the Action reports a failed review instead of reviewing the PR. The prior 64 MiB limit explicitly supported these patch sizes.

findings.title: Restore the explicit read-only Codex sandbox
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing `-s read-only` delegates filesystem permissions to Codex's effective defaults/configuration. Since the agent is launched with `cwd: opts.repoPath` and receives the supplied prompt, prompt injection from reviewed content can cause it to alter the checkout rather than only inspect it.

findings.title: Build the review diff from the PR head SHA
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_HEAD_SHA is supplied and the checkout HEAD differs (for example, a PR merge-ref checkout), the patch and changed-file set describe HEAD while the submitted review is attached to headSha. This can review/comment on merge-result changes rather than the PR head commit.

findings.title: Keep prompt payloads literal during replacement
findings.whyItBreaks: String.prototype.replace interprets `$&`, `$`` and `$'` in a string replacement. bundle.patch is arbitrary diff content, so a normal patch containing `$&` causes the critic prompt to retain `{{PATCH}}` instead of the patch; other tokens splice portions of the prompt into the JSON payload. The same corruption can affect serialized bundle and candidate content. The previous callback replacements inserted these values literally.

findings.title: Keep fallback review pinned to the analyzed commit
findings.whyItBreaks: When the JSON review request fails and a new commit is pushed while review() is running, omitting commit_id makes GitHub default the fallback review to the PR's then-current head. The review body and verdict were computed from headSha captured at src/adapters/github.ts:141, so a REQUEST_CHANGES review can be associated with code that was never reviewed.

findings.title: Keep malformed findings distinguishable from real findings
findings.whyItBreaks: Invalid severity/category, missing required text, and invalid or absent line numbers previously caused normalization to fail. They now become a plausible P1 bug at line 0 with empty metadata, so callers cannot distinguish malformed model output from a real review finding and may publish or act on fabricated findings.

findings.title: Keep explicit repository when resolving manually dispatched PRs
findings.whyItBreaks: The workflow_dispatch path reaches these commands before any checkout. Without -R "$REPO", gh pr view must infer a repository from the runner's current Git worktree; a clean self-hosted workspace has no checkout yet, so ref resolution fails and the subsequent checkout receives no head/base SHA.

findings.title: Reject malformed review payloads instead of defaulting them
findings.whyItBreaks: Missing or wrongly typed required fields now produce an empty RawReview rather than the prior error. In particular, a failed/invalid review response with no findings is indistinguishable from a valid clean review, so downstream consumers can treat unusable model output as a successful pass. This exported normalizer exposes that conflated failure contract even though this minimal repository has no in-repo callers.

findings.title: Restore PR ref resolution for manual dispatches
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, the event has no pull_request object, so both expressions evaluate empty. The job now checks out github.ref (the branch from which the workflow was dispatched) and fetches main, rather than the requested pr_number's head/base; the review invocation consequently receives empty PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA. The previous Resolve PR refs step specifically queried these values with gh for this event type.

findings.title: Restore the Git diff output buffer limit
findings.whyItBreaks: Without maxBuffer, spawnSync uses Node's 1 MiB default. runLocal obtains the entire patch through git(["diff", baseSha, "HEAD"]) at line 100, so a repository diff exceeding 1 MiB causes spawnSync to fail and prevents the review from running. The previous 64 MiB limit explicitly supported such diffs.

findings.title: Publish review errors as failures
findings.whyItBreaks: Any exception from fetching the PR, obtaining its diff, or running the review reaches this handler. Posting `neutral` instead of the previous `failure` makes the Needlefish check successful for GitHub required-status-check purposes, so a PR can merge even though the review explicitly did not run or pass.

findings.title: Keep the reviewer executable on trusted main
findings.whyItBreaks: The workflow checks out the PR head at lines 43-47, then runs its src/cli.ts here with GH_TOKEN (line 56) and pull-requests/checks write permissions (lines 18-19). An internal malicious PR can modify the reviewer or its installed dependency metadata to fabricate a passing review or use the token to write PR/check results, bypassing the review gate. Previously the executable was independently checked out from frankekn/needlefish@main.

facts.meaning: The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.

findings.title: Preserve canonicalization of severity values
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview accepts untyped raw review output and passes each finding here. A valid severity emitted with casing or whitespace variation, such as "p0" or " P1 ", previously normalized to P0/P1 but now fails the exact-match check and becomes P3. This silently downgrades real findings instead of preserving their intended severity.

findings.title: Keep GitHub tokens out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: Omitting `env` causes `spawnSync` to inherit `process.env`. The previous implementation explicitly removed `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `GITHUB_API_TOKEN`; those credentials are now available to the externally invoked `codex` binary and its tool-executed subprocesses. A repository-controlled prompt or untrusted tool invocation can therefore read and exfiltrate credentials even though the Codex sandbox is configured read-only.

findings.title: Restore the same-repository guard before running PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the job-level condition makes pull requests from forks eligible for this self-hosted job. The workflow checks out the fork's head SHA, runs its dependency installation, then executes its src/cli.ts while the job has pull-requests: write and checks: write permissions. A fork author can alter package scripts, dependencies, or the CLI to execute arbitrary commands on the runner and use the available token to modify PR/check state.

findings.title: Allow zero-valued runner grace configuration
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, setting either NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 or NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 was accepted and passed directly to its timer. This change rejects zero and silently substitutes 5000 ms or 2000 ms, respectively. Upgrading therefore makes an explicitly configured immediate escalation wait seconds before SIGKILL or before returning a timeout result.

findings.title: Keep deep-review failures as blocking residual risks
findings.whyItBreaks: A malformed or failed runCodex call for any one hotspot now rejects reviewLarge entirely. Previously the failure was converted into a blocking residual risk and the remaining review/critic pass could return a structured result.

findings.title: Preserve residual risks reported by deep review
findings.whyItBreaks: Successful deep passes can report blocking residual_risks when they cannot establish safety. This code replaces all of them with [], so the critic cannot distinguish "no risks" from "unreviewable hotspot" and may return PASS for an incompletely reviewed large PR.

findings.title: Deep-review every changed file after hotspot truncation
findings.whyItBreaks: Only the first six risk-ranked hotspots are processed. A large PR with more than six distinct mapped surfaces leaves every file assigned solely to later hotspots without a deep review; the critic receives only patchStat, not their patch content.

findings.title: Preserve focus in large-review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: The removed {{FOCUS}} substitution means reviewLarge no longer supplies bundle.focus to any deep hotspot review. A focused large PR therefore produces an unfocused review, unlike the small-review path which still serializes the complete bundle.

findings.title: Normalize rounded seconds into minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: For 119500ms, minutes is computed as 1 and seconds rounds from 59.5 to 60, so rendered output is `1m 60s` instead of `2m 0s`. The prior total-seconds calculation correctly carried the rounding overflow.

findings.title: Reject zero in the positive-integer parser
findings.whyItBreaks: `parsePositiveInteger("0", label)` now returns `0`, despite its public name and error contract requiring a positive integer. Consumers can therefore receive zero where validation promises a value greater than zero.
